# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the defusal manual, which states:
- The light continuously cycles through five colors every round.
- What matters is the light's color at the moment of the cut.
- Defusal rules:
  - red light -> cut yellow wire
  - white light -> cut green wire
  - yellow light -> cut blue wire

Since I cannot speak, I can only send gestures to Deaf. Deaf cannot hear, but can speak to Blind and see my gestures. Blind can hear Deaf and cut the wires, but cannot see.

Because "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something" and Deaf has not yet spoken or set up a gesture convention, any gesture I send now would have no agreed-upon meaning. Deaf goes third this round, can see the bomb, and will speak to describe the setup and establish how I should signal.

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to speak.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can hear speech and cut wires 1 to 3, but I cannot see gestures. Deaf can speak and see gestures. Please have Deaf speak the bomb details (display, light, wires) to you, check your manual, gesture the wire number to Deaf (1, 2, or 3), and have Deaf speak to me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb state: Display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires are 1: blue, 2: green, 3: yellow. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do, and I will speak it to Blind.

I need to know the light cycle and make sure Blind does not cut until the light matches a condition in the manual. In Round 1 the light was blue (not in the table: red -> cut yellow, white -> cut green, yellow -> cut blue). Since the light changes every round in a five-color cycle, we must wait, observe the cycle, and time the cut for the exact round where the light matches the target wire. Gesturing a stop/wait hand signal to Deaf will prevent Blind from cutting prematurely and prompt Deaf to report the light's next color.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Display is 0. Light has changed to yellow (was blue). Wires are 1: blue, 2: green, 3: yellow. Blind, remember I am deaf and cannot hear you, but Mute can hear you. Mute gestured ✋ to me. Mute, to avoid ambiguity, let us use these gestures: ☝ = cut wire 1, ✌ = cut wire 2, 🤟 = cut wire 3, ✊ = push/hold button, 🫳 = release button, ✋ = wait/do nothing, 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Mute, please gesture what Blind should do now.

We need to know the light cycle to predict which round will have a valid light color for the cut (since Blind acts before Deaf in each round, any instruction from Deaf to Blind is received for the subsequent round). 

In Round 1 the light was blue. In Round 2 the light was yellow. Deaf will observe the Round 3 light at the end of this round. Deaf established ✋ as "wait/do nothing". Therefore, I gesture ✋ so Deaf tells Blind to wait and reports the new light color.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Display is 0. Light is now RED (history: Turn 1 blue, Turn 2 yellow, Turn 3 red). Wires are 1: blue, 2: green, 3: yellow. Mute gestured ✋ (wait). Blind, hold on and do nothing yet. Mute, when the moment is right, gesture the action.

To confirm the 5-colour cycle and properly time the defusal cut, we must wait through the remaining colours of the first cycle. Wire 1 (blue) corresponds to yellow light, which will reappear on Turn 7. I will signal to wait.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Display is 0. Light is now WHITE (history: blue -> yellow -> red -> white). Wires: 1: blue, 2: green, 3: yellow. Mute gestured ✋ again. Blind, continue to wait.

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Display is 0. Light is now GREEN (history: blue -> yellow -> red -> white -> green). Wires: 1: blue, 2: green, 3: yellow. Mute gestured ✋. Blind, continue waiting.

We know the light cycle:
Turn 1: Blue
Turn 2: Yellow
Turn 3: Red
Turn 4: White
Turn 5: Green
Turn 6: Blue
Turn 7: Yellow

The manual rules:
- red light -> cut yellow wire
- white light -> cut green wire
- yellow light -> cut blue wire

Wires on the bomb:
1: blue
2: green
3: yellow

In Round 7, the light will be Yellow.
Under Yellow light, the blue wire must be cut.
The blue wire is Wire 1.

The turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
In Round 6:
- Mute gestures ☝ (cut wire 1) to Deaf.
- Deaf receives the gesture at the end of Round 6 and speaks to Blind telling Blind to cut wire 1.
- In Round 7, Blind hears Deaf's instruction and cuts Wire 1 while the light is Yellow.

Therefore, the gesture to send Deaf now is ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, action now! Mute gestured ☝, which means CUT WIRE 1. Cut wire 1 (the first wire / blue wire) now!

I have provided the instruction, which Deaf transmitted to Blind. Blind will now cut wire 1 during this round while the light is yellow, matching the manual's rule. I will wait.

```
wait()
```
